Blake Snell says pressure is not a concern ahead of crucial Game 3 start
Dodgers pitcher Blake Snell says he's unfazed by high stakes ahead of Game 3 at Dodger Stadium after two losses against Milwaukee. Despite injuries limiting his season appearances this year, Snell remains focused as Los Angeles seeks its third straight championship.
Los Angeles Dodgers starting pitcher Blake Snell is set to take the mound in an important Game 3 at Dodger Stadium on Oct. 14, but said he is not letting the situation affect him.
The Dodgers lost the first two games of the series in Milwaukee, making Game 3 critical as they pursue a third consecutive championship. Snell credited the Brewers' improvement since last year's National League Championship Series, which the Dodgers swept, but said this year's circumstances are different.
"I don’t think about last year because it has nothing to do with this year and it’s a completely different team," Snell said. "Just from experience, growth, mindset, discipline, where they’re at… Even the way [Brewers manager Pay Murphy]’s talking is way different than how he was talking last year.
"It’s a completely different team, I’m well aware of that. This game, and what it means to me, it hasn’t changed. 0-2, 2-0, it doesn’t matter. I know what I need to do to win and dominate and I’m going to just focus on that. …I think they’re in a good spot now, especially being up 2-0, but adversity hits and that’s when thoughts start racing."
Snell's season was shortened by injuries in 2026 but he recorded strong results over his ten starts. He posted a 1.90 earned run average across nine starts in the second half of the season with 55 strikeouts over 42.2 innings pitched.
In his only postseason start so far this year against Atlanta in the Division Series—a game which marked Los Angeles' only loss—Snell allowed one run but walked five batters while pitching just three and two-thirds innings.
Last year against Milwaukee in Game One of the NLCS, Snell threw eight scoreless innings on the road with ten strikeouts and allowed only one hit. The Dodgers will look for another steady performance from him as they try to stay alive in their pursuit of another World Series title.
